items.e: **MISHNAH:** An onion which one added to lentils, if whole it is permitted, if cut up it depends on transferring taste. Any other cooked food, whether whole or cut up, depends on transferring taste. Rebbi Jehudah permits in anchovies where it only serves to remove pollutants. If a mashed apple is added to dough and it soured, [the dough] is forbidden. But if barley grains fell into a cistern of water, even though they made it stink, [the water] is permitted.

**HALAKHAH:** “An onion which one added to lentils,” etc. Rebbi Ḥizqiah, Rav Aḥa in the name of Rebbi Abba bar Mamal said, our Mishnah [in case] after the lentils lost their sap; [then] the lentils shrink it so it will not absorb [any taste]. (As you say, lentils shrink it so it will not absorb.) Similarly, lentils shrink it so it will not give.

The Mishnah speaks about a profane onion which he put into heave lentils; but not the case of a heave onion put into profane lentils. If it is dry, but moist is forbidden. An onion, but leeks are forbidden moist or dry, entire or cut up.

If he removed the tip it is as if cut up. If there were two or three small ones, they are as if cut up. Only if the outer shell does not transmit taste. But if the outer shell transmits taste, it is forbidden.

There, we have stated: “If fish improved in value when cooked with leeks of second tithe, the increase is proportional.” Rebbi Hoshaia said, that Mishnah does not follow Rebbi Jehudah, since we have stated: “Rebbi Jehudah permits in anchovies where it only serves to remove pollutants.”

The rabbis of Caesarea asked: The saying of Rebbi Abbahu in the name of Rebbi Joḥanan, that all forbidden [food] is estimated as if it were onion, as if it were leeks, does this contradict Rebbi Jehudah? Rebbi Jehudah will agree regarding an onion of the Temple or an onion of idol worship.

“If a mashed apple is added to dough which soured, [the dough] is forbidden” It was stated: Rebbi Yose permits it. Rebbi Aḥa, Rebbi Abbahu in the name of Rebbi Yose ben Ḥanina: They disagree when it becomes sour from the juice [of the apple]. But if it becomes sour from its solid substance it is permitted. Just as Rebbi Yose says there, its souring is not clearly souring, so he says here, its cooking is not clearly cooking.

“Everything that can be smelled is forbidden, whether it improves or spoils, the words of Rebbi Meїr. Rebbi Simeon says, if it improves it is forbidden, if it spoils it is permitted.” Rebbi Simeon ben Laqish said, in what do they disagree? If it first improved but then spoiled. But if it spoiled and later improved, even Rebbi Meїr will agree. Rebbi Joḥanan said, there is no difference whether it spoiled and improved or improved and spoiled, it is a disagreement. There, we have stated: “If barley grains fell into a cistern of water, even though they made it stink, the water is permitted.” What is the status of that Mishnah? Rebbi Joḥanan said it is a disagreement; Rebbi Simeon ben Laqish said it is the opinion of everybody. Rebbi Yose ben Rebbi Abun said this tradition here: Rebbi Joḥanan said it is a disagreement; Rebbi Simeon ben Laqish said it is the opinion of everybody.

**MISHNAH:** If somebody takes hot pitta bread out of the oven and deposits it on the mouth of an amphora of heave wine, Rebbi Meїr forbids and Rebbi Jehudah permits. Rebbi Yose permits in the case of wheat and forbids in the case of barley because barley absorbs. If an oven was heated with heave cumin and one baked bread in it, the bread is permitted since it absorbs not the taste of cumin but the smell of cumin.

**HALAKHAH:** Rebbi Zeїra said, they asked before Rebbi Yannai: What [are the rules] if he put it on the plug of the amphora? He said to them ( Job 36:33 ): “Its neighbor will inform about it.” What means, “its neighbor will inform about it”? Rebbi Yose said, that which we have stated there: “An amphora full of fruits added to fluids, or one full of fluids added to fruits.” As you say there, only if the fluids touch the amphora; so here only if the loaf touches the plug. Rebbi Mana said, from this it follows as you say there, only if the fluids touch the amphora itself; so here only if the loaf touches the plug itself. His opinion implies, even [if the pitta] is cold. Rebbi Abba said, the problem was about a cold one. But did we not state “hot”? Rav Ḥisda said, that one should not say since the vapor absorbs it should be permitted.

Following Rebbi Simeon ben Laqish, water acts on fruits, [other] fluids do not act on fruits, against Rebbi Jehudah! But Rebbi Simeon ben Laqish says, water acts on fruits and loses fluid volume, [other] fluids act on fruits and do not lose volume. Rebbi Jehudah says, [other] fluids do not act on fruits at all.

And what Rebbi Joḥanan said, when we went to Caesarea to study Torah with the Great Rebbi Hoshaia, we put our flat-cake on boxes of fish sauce and we tasted there the taste of fish sauce. Is this against Rebbi Jehudah? They put it into the brine. Is that not forbidden because they rob the owner? They had obtained the owner’s permission.
Wheat below and barley above; just as wheat does not absorb so the barley will not absorb. Barley below and wheat above, just as barley absorbs so wheat will absorb.

May one roast two spits together in one oven, one of kosher meat and one of carcass meat? Rav Jeremiah said in the name of Rav, it is forbidden. Samuel said in the name of Levi, it is permitted. A baraita disagrees with Rav: “One may not roast two Passover sacrifices together in one oven because they could be mixed up.” They said only, because they could be mixed up; therefore, not if they could not be mixed up.
Calamint water, Rav said it is forbidden, Samuel said it is permitted. Samuel served Rav calamint water.
That inner part, Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi in the name of Rav: One fires it with dry branches.

**MISHNAH:** Fenugreek that fell into a water cistern, for heave and second tithe if the seeds are enough to impart taste, disregarding the wood. But for the Sabbatical, kilaim in a vineyard, and dedicated seeds, if seeds and wood together impart taste. If somebody had bundles of fenugreek of kilaim from a vineyard, they should be burned. If he had bundles of fenugreek from ṭevel , he pounds them and computes how much seed this contains and separates the seeds but not the wood. If he separated, he should not say I shall pound, take the wood, and give the seeds but he gives seeds with the wood.

**HALAKHAH:** Does not the wood spoil repeatedly? Our Mishnah follows him who says that anything that spoils is forbidden. But even according to him who says anything that spoils is permitted, he agrees here that it is forbidden. Why? Fenugreek improves anything into which it falls.
How much is a bundle? 25 plants. Rebbi Joḥanan said, four to a bed.

It implies that they become ṭevel in bundles. Why not single ears? One never gathers for that. But may grains be gathered thus? One does not grow for that. But these, one gathers for this, one grows for this.

**MISHNAH:** Profane olives preserved with heave olives, if they were broken profanes with broken heaves, broken profanes with whole heaves, or preserves in heave fluid, are forbidden. But whole profanes with broken heaves are permitted.

**HALAKHAH:** Rebbi Jonah said, this implies that broken [olives] absorb, release, and absorb again; whole [olives] absorb, release, but do not absorb again. That means, if it is neither improving nor spoiling it is forbidden. The Mishnah is Rebbi Simeon’s, for Rebbi Simeon says if its taste spoils, it is forbidden. But did Rebbi Simeon not say, if its taste spoils, it is permitted? Following what Rebbi Simeon says, irrigated cabbage preserved with unirrigated cabbage is forbidden because it absorbs.

**MISHNAH:** If an impure fish was preserved with a pure fish, if in any keg containing two seah the impure fish weighed ten zuz in Judea which are five tetradrachmas in Galilee, the sauce is forbidden. Rebbi Jehudah says, a quarter [ log ] in two seah . Rebbi Yose said, one sixteenth of it. Impure locusts preserved with pure locusts do not forbid the fluid exuding from the latter. Rebbi Ẓadoq testified that the fluid exuding from impure locusts is pure.

**HALAKHAH:** Rebbi Jehudah bar Pazi stated from Bar Delaiah: “Unsalted pure fish preserved with salted impure fish is forbidden”. But did we not state: “He washes it and it is permitted”? Rebbi Mana said, he who said it is permitted, when he preserved them simultaneously; he who said it is prohibited when he preserved them one after the other. You can understand that this is so, since we have stated “in heave fluid it is forbidden;” [is that] not when he preserved one after the other?

“Any keg containing two seah ”. How much is in a seah ? [24] (14) log . How much is in a log ? 2 pounds. How much is in a pound? 100 zin . It turns out that each single zin corresponds to one in 960. Rebbi Yose ben Rebbi Abun instructed at Akhbara: one in a thousand.

Rebbi Abbahu in the name of Rebbi Yose bar Ḥanina: A quarter [ log ] of fish sauce in two seah of fish sauce. But the sauce of an impure fish never can save! Rebbi Abbahu said, I computed that close to 200. Rebbi Ila in the name of Rebbi Simeon bar Ḥiyya, a quarter [ log ] of fish sauce in two seah of fish and fish sauce. A case came before Rebbi Joshia and he instructed accordingly.

We have stated thus: “When has this been said? If he scoops out piece by piece and puts them before himself, he has to proceed in the way indicated. But if he scoops out piece by piece and throws them away, even more than was indicated is permitted.”

By some pretext, cheese was mixed up. Rebbi Ḥaggai asked Rebbi Abba bar Zavda. He said to them, the property of the public cannot be forbidden. Rebbi Jacob bar Zavdi said, Rebbi Isaac asked: Is not Caius Lycus written on these documents, and you say, by a pretext?
“Rebbi Ẓadoq testified that the fluid exuding from impure locusts is pure.” In what respect is it pure? It is pure not to prepare. But to make impure, the most minute amount makes impure.

**MISHNAH:** All those which are pickled one with the other are permitted except with bulb plants. Profane bulb plant with heave bulb plant, profane vegetable with heave bulb plant, are forbidden. But profane bulb plant with heave vegetable is permitted. Rebbi Yose says, all that is cooked in water with white beets is forbidden because it imparts taste. Rebbi Simeon says, irrigated cabbage [preserved] with unirrigated cabbage is forbidden because it absorbs. Rebbi Aqiba says, all those which are cooked together are permitted except with meat. Rebbi Yose says, all that is cooked in water with white beets is forbidden because it imparts taste. Rebbi Simeon says, irrigated cabbage [preserved] with unirrigated cabbage is forbidden because it absorbs. Rebbi Aqiba says, all those which are cooked together are permitted except with meat. If an egg was treated with forbidden spices, even its yolk is forbidden because it absorbs. Pickling and cooking fluid of heave is forbidden to laymen.
**HALAKHAH:** Rebbi Joḥanan said, one does not speak of pickled [food] but of that cooked in water. Pickled is like being hot.

Rebbi Ḥanina Tortayya in the name of Rebbi Hoshaiah: Bulb vegetables with bulb vegetables, a kind with itself, Rebbi Aqiba permits but the Sages forbid. Rebbi Assi in the name of Rebbi Joḥanan: The Sages agree with Rebbi Aqiba that meat with meat is permitted. Rebbi Zeїra said to Rebbi Assi: If that had not been said, we would not know that it is so, but maybe it was said as follows: Rebbi Aqiba agrees with the Sages that meat with meat is forbidden. Rebbi Abbahu came in the name of Rebbi Joḥanan: Rebbi Aqiba agrees with the Sages that meat with meat is forbidden. Rebbi Ḥinena understood it from the next Mishnah: “Rebbi Aqiba says, all those which are cooked together are permitted except with meat.” Therefore, “meat with meat is forbidden.” Maybe it was formulated as: The Sages agree with Rebbi Aqiba that meat with meat is forbidden. Rebbi Ḥinena: Rebbi Abbahu in the name of Rebbi Joḥanan, the Sages agree with Rebbi Aqiba that meat with meat is forbidden.
Rebbi Yose said, we were of the opinion that the unirrigated [cabbage] absorbs. Since Rav Huna said, take away its growing parts and get moisture; this shows that the irrigated absorbs.
Rebbi Jeremiah asked: What is the rule if he cooked it in milk? Rebbi Zeїra never in his life ate liver. Rebbi Abba cooked it in water and ate it; some say Rebbi Abba salted and ate it.
“Yolk is forbidden because it absorbs.” Bar Qappara stated: Yolk is forbidden and certainly egg white.
Isaac Rabba in the name of Rebbi Simeon ben Laqish: If eggs were cooked in water and a chick was found in one of them, it is [judged] by the taste it gives.

Rebbi Zeїra, Rebbi Simeon bar Abba in the name of Rebbi Joḥanan; Ada bar Gershon, Rebbi Birai, Rebbi Levi bar Plautus, an elder in the name of Rebbi: 61 are forbidden, 62 are permitted. Rebbi Samuel bar Naḥman in the name of Rebbi Jonathan: Our colleague Ada testified before us: 60. He said, if somebody brings before me more than 60, I shall declare it kosher. They said to Simeon bar Abba, you say this, but the others say otherwise! He said to them, I [said] what I heard, they what they heard. Simeon bar Abba said before Rebbi Ḥanina in the name of the elder Rebbi Ḥiyya: Up to thirty. He said, an exaggeration. Simeon bar Abba in the name of Rebbi Ḥanina: A case came before Rabban Gamliel ben Rabbi. He said, my father did not agree to 47, I agree to 45. Rebbi Ḥiyya in the name of Rebbi Ḥanina: A case came before Rebbi; he asked: Are there 50?

Rebbi Ḥiyya in the name of Rebbi Ḥanina: Vegetables, shells, and water are counted. Rebbi Zeїra said, even if the inside is forbidden. Rav Huna said, the shells of the forbidden help the permitted. Rebbi Zeїra: That is, if he cooked them in their shells, cooked with cooked. But if he cooked shelled eggs with unshelled in water, or unshelled with shelled, cooked with uncooked, that needs a different measure.

Unimpregnated eggs are permitted: ( Job 21:10 ) “His steer made pregnant, he will not miss impregnating.” Eggs that started developing are forbidden. Twisted ones, he who likes it may eat them. If one found blood in them, one shaves off the place of the blood.

Rebbi Zeїra went to visit Rebbi Ḥiyya, the son of Rebbi Isaac Aṭoshiyya. He found him sitting. He said, they taught only for yolk, but in the egg white it is permitted. He thought that he had heard it from his ancestor. Rebbi Abbahu came in the name of Rebbi Joḥanan: Both egg white and yolk are forbidden. Rebbi Ḥalaphta ben Shaul stated: Yolk is forbidden, egg white permitted. Rebbi Zeїra said, he who says yolk is forbidden if it is found at the male part of the yolk; this applies even to yolk, but only if it is found on its male part since from there the development of the chick starts.

There, we have stated: “The following disable and do not fill: Water, whether pure or impure, pickling water, cooking water, afterwine before it became vinegar.” Here, you treat it as food, there as fluid. Rebbi Mana said, here when it is thick, there when it is thin. Rebbi Yose ben Rebbi Abun said, you may even say in both cases thick or thin. Taste counts for heave but not for a miqweh .
